newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: COSTA RICA EASES OIL EXPLORATION TERMS.
newsitem.headline: COSTA RICA EASES OIL EXPLORATION TERMS.

text.p: Costa Rica has eased the terms of its first ever oil and gas exploration licensing round in the hope of kindling more interest in the oil-poor country, a government spokesman said on Thursday. Commercial quantities of oil have never been found in Costa Rica, but in February it offered 25 blocks for licensing to national and international firms in the hope of cashing in on a surge in international exploration investment.

The Environment and Energy Ministry spokesman said no bids had yet been received, but 10 information packs were sold at a cost of $1,000 each and the Ministry extended the bid deadline from July 14 to December 10.

The participation fee was lowered from 10 to five percent of total planned investment, the minimum seismic study was set at 150 kilometres (100 miles) per block instead of 150-450 kilometres, and the minimum drilling has been cut from 1,500 metres (5,000 feet) per block to 750 metres (2,500 feet). The blocks include Pacific and Caribbean areas, both onshore and offshore.
Oil exploration began in Costa Rica in 1915, but was suspended in 1988 without any significant reserves being found.
